newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on election, inflation hope.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on election, inflation hope.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 90 basis points to 18.90 percent in early trade on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market shrugged off liquidity pressures on continuing euphoria following Sunday's relatively peaceful mid-term elections and optimistic forecasts for inflation data due later today.
"The market is still on a roll over the elections... Furthermore, inflation figures are due any time and look like they will be low," a fixed-income analyst said.
Banco de Mxico was expected to release consumer inflation data shortly before the close of money market trading.
A Reuters survey of 13 financial firms in Mexico MEX22 revealed an average forecast increase of 0.90 percent in the consumer price index for June, compared to 0.91 percent in the prior month.
Analysts said they had expected liquidity pressures as Wednesday sees the monthly deadline for banks to settle outstanding balances on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Foreign capital flows had, nonetheless, outweighed pressure from the central bank cut-off date, they added.
"The cut-off will soak up some liquidity, but we expect a quiet session with stable rates due to foreign investors stepping into the market," one analyst said.
Dealers meanwhile said rates had fallen in line with Tuesday night's auction results and due to a strong peso.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 18.37 percent at its weekly auction, a fall of 158 basis points since last week.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile 60 basis points lower at 19.40 percent.
Liquidity of 707 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
